title: Purification and Analytics of a Monoclonal Antibody from Chinese Hamster Ovary Cells Using an Automated Microbioreactor System
protocol: Open the software attached to the purification system.
Equilibrate the column with equilibration buffer at a flow rate of 2 mL/min for 40 min using manual instructions.
Stop the manual run after equilibration.
Place 15 mL conical tubes in the fraction collector to collect purified antibody eluate and 50 mL conical tubes to collect flow-through during high salt wash.
Reset the fraction collector to the start position by opening and closing it before beginning the run.
Maintain the fraction collector at 7 °C.
Add the 0.22 µm filtered harvest cell culture fluid to an empty 12 mL syringe whose nozzle end is capped.
Holding the syringe with the nozzle facing down, insert the syringe plunger till a small portion is in.
Turn the syringe with the nozzle facing up and remove the cap.
Push the cylinder to dispel any air until the fluid is at the tip of the nozzle.
Insert the syringe nozzle into the manual injection port on the purification system and twist to tighten.
Push down on the plunger until all the sample is injected.
Open the saved method file.
Save the result file in the required location and specify the file name when prompted.
Hit run after the sample has been injected into the large volume sample loop.
Equilibrate the column with three column volumes of equilibration buffer at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Wash the column with equilibration buffer at a flow rate of 2 mL/min until the UV signal drops below 25 mAU.
Use four column volumes (CVs) of 25 mM Tris with 1 M NaCl at pH 7.5 for a secondary high salt wash at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.
Collect any protein/DNA that comes off the column during the salt wash in 50 mL tubes using the system fraction collector.
Apply five CVs of elution buffer at a flow rate of 1 mL/min to elute the antibody off the column.
Start collecting the eluate in 15 mL tubes when the UV 280 signal is above 35 mAU and stop collection when the signal drops below 50 mAU.
Wash the column using three CVs of equilibration buffer after elution.
Immediately neutralize the purified protein using 1 M Tris base to a pH of ~5.5 after the wash step.
Measure the protein concentration using a microvolume UV-Vis spectrophotometer at 280 nm and 260 nm.
Store the measured protein at 4 °C.
Concentrate the purified antibody using centrifugal units.
Subject the purified antibody to glycan analysis using LC-MS.
Analyze the aggregation profile of the purified antibody using SEC-MALS.
Insert 100 kDa filters into centrifuge tubes.
Wash the filters with 500 µL of double distilled water.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 14,000 x g at room temperature (RT).
Repeat washing step twice.
Discard filtrate.
Transfer rinsed filters to fresh centrifuge tubes and add 500 µL of sample to each filter.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 14,000 x g.
Invert the filter into a fresh spin tube.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 1,000 x g to collect concentrated sample.
Determine sample concentrations using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Blank the spectrophotometer using Tris-acetate buffer.
Use a protein extinction coefficient of 1.37 mL•(mg•cm)-1 at 280 nm for a 1% (% m/v) IgG solution.
Prepare 12.5 µL of 2 mg/mL working solution for glycan analysis.
Prepare 30 µL of 3.5 mg/mL working solution for SEC-MALS.
Dilute 7.5 μL of antibodies with 15.3 μL of LC-MS-grade water in 1 mL tubes provided with the kit.
Denature the samples using 6 μL of a 5% enzyme-friendly and MS-friendly surfactant at 90 °C for 3 min.
Cool the denatured samples to room temperature (RT) for 3 min.
Add 1.2 μL of PNGase F and incubate for 5 min at 50 °C.
Cool the samples to RT for 3 min after incubation with PNGase F.
Label the cleaved N-glycans by adding 12 μL of fluorescent tagging reagent dissolved in anhydrous dimethylformamide (DMF).
Wait for 5 min after adding the fluorescent tagging reagent.
Dilute the labeled N-glycan mixture with 358 μL of acetonitrile (ACN).
Place a hydrophilic interaction chromatography (HILIC) plate in a vacuum manifold with shims and waste tray.
Condition the HILIC wells with 200 µL of water, allowing liquid to pass through the resin for 15-30 s under vacuum.
Equilibrate the wells with 200 μL of 85% ACN prior to loading the ACN-diluted labeled glycan mixture (400 µL).
Apply a vacuum after each new liquid is added to the HILIC resin.
Wash the HILIC resin with 600 µL of 1% formic acid (FA)/90% ACN twice.
Replace the waste tray with 600 µL collection tubes.
Elute labeled N-glycans with SPE elution buffer in three steps of 30 µL each.
Dilute pooled elutions with 310 µL of DMF/ACN sample diluent.
Pipette samples into auto sampler vials for fluorescence (FLR)-MS analysis.
Store the HILIC plate taped shut and inside a desiccator for future use.
Analyze labeled N-glycan elution samples on an Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography (UPLC) system coupled to a fluorescence detector and quadrupole time-of-flight (Q-ToF) mass spectrometer.
Flush column with 60% acetonitrile and 40% H2O: 50 CVs before the first use or 20 CVs if previously used.
Use 50 mM ammonium formate (AmF) and 100% LC-MS-grade ACN for mobile phases.
Set initial flow rate to 0.4 mL/min.
Provide increasing AmF during the elution phase using an LC gradient.
Set the FLR detector to measure at EX 265/EM 425 nm with a sampling rate of 2 Hz.
Set the Q-ToF to MS1 positive ion sensitivity mode, with a mass range of 100-2,000 daltons (Da), a scan time of 0.25 seconds and continuum data acquisition.
Use leucine enkephalin (2 ng/µL in 50% ACN/0.1% FA) for the internal mass reference, in the "Do NOT apply correction" mode.
Re-suspend the dextran ladder sequentially in 22.5 µL of H2O, then in 25 µL of DMF, and finally in 52.5 µL of ACN.
Prepare 10 µL aliquots for storage at -80 °C.
Place the samples in the auto sampler set to 10 °C.
Load a vial of dextran ladder along with samples.
Inject samples in triplicate, using 10 µL injections for the samples and 7.5 µL injections for the ladder.
Run the loaded method.
Perform data processing with a program optimized for hydrophilic interaction chromatography fluorescence mass spectrometry (HILIC-FLR-MS) data.
Apply internal mass reference corrections within the program.
Designate the dextran ladder injections as "Standard" in Sample Information.
Set the Separation Compound retention times to those of the ladder compounds detected during the run in the Analysis Method.
Modify the Analysis Method: Under the Processing tab, click Quantitation Settings - Calibrate and set "Calibration curve fit type" to "Relative response (%)".
Transfer 3.5 mg/mL diluted protein to a vial with a 150 µL glass insert.
Use a gel loading tip to pipet into the bottom bell of the insert to avoid introducing bubbles.
Cap the vial with a septa cap and analyze immediately or store at 4 °C if analyzing later.
Configure SEC-MALS with an Ultra High-Pressure Liquid Chromatography (UHPLC) system equipped with a MALS Detector and Refractive Index Detector controlled by the MALS software.
Configure a method file in the UHPLC software for control of the UHPLC system.
Set the flow rate to 0.4 mL/min with a mobile phase of 1x Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS).
Set the injection volume to 5 μL.
Set the column temperature to 25 °C.
Set the Diode Array Detector (DAD) to monitor 280 nm.
Set run time to 20 min.
Equilibrate the system for at least 4 h prior to any sample analysis.
Turn on the DAD lamp 30 min prior to beginning analysis.
Set the wavelength to 280 nm in the DAD method file.
Purge the Refractive Index (RI) reference cell for 15 min or until the baseline is stable and then close the reference cell.
Configure SEC-MALS software sequence, setting the collection time to 12 min.
Set the injection volume to 5 μL.
Set the dn/dc to 0.185 mL/g.
Set the A280 extinction coefficient if previously experimentally determined or to 1.37 mL*(mg*cm)-1.
Set the concentration of the sample.
Click Run and wait for the "waiting to inject" dialog to appear on the screen.
Configure a sample list in the UHPLC software in the same order as in MALS-RI software.
Submit the sample list.
Start with 80 μL of a 3.5 mg/mL antibody solution for sample preparation and labeling.
Desalt the sample using a 0.5 mL Desalting Column (7k MWCO).
Prepare the column by first snapping off the bottom stopper, then loosening the top stopper, and placing it in a 1.7 mL micro-centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the desalting column for 1 min at 1,500 x g.
Transfer the column to a new micro-centrifuge tube.
Add 80 µL of diluted protein to the top of the column.
Align the column to the original orientation.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 1,500 x g.
Remove the sample from the centrifuge.
Discard the desalting column.
Mix the sample well.
Dilute the sample to a final concentration of 2 mg/mL in a volume of 25 µL.
Add 5 µL of labeling buffer to the 96-well plate.
Prepare the labeling reagent by diluting it 1:30 in dimethylformamide.
Incubate the sample for 10 min at room temperature away from light.
Add 60 µL of reagent grade water to the sample.
Mix well by pipetting.
Cover the plate with a plate seal.
Centrifuge the plate at 1,000 x g for 1 min.
Remove storage solution from Charge Variant chip.
Wash wells 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, and 10 with water.
Replace the water in washed wells with pH 7.2 running buffer.
Add 750 µL of pH 7.2 running buffer to the buffer tube.
Place the buffer tube in the indicated spot on the upper left-hand corner of the sample tray.
Remove the plate seal from the 96-well plate.
Press Unload Plate on the instrument user interface.
Insert the plate into the GXII sample tray.
Press the Unload Chip button on the user interface.
Ensure that the electrodes are free of any particles.
Clean the electrodes with a lint-free swab if necessary.
Check that the window in the center of the chip is free of particles or smudges.
Clean the window with a lint-free soft cloth if necessary.
Close the lid to the chip chamber.
Select the HT Protein Charge Variant assay.
Click the Run button.
Follow the prompts to select the sample wells, plate type, and assay time (68, 90, or 100 s).
Enter a file name as prompted.
Click Start at the end of the prompts.
Wash each well twice with water for chip cleanup.
Add Storage Buffer to each well after washing.
Replace the chip in the instrument.
Select the HT Protein Charge assay when prompted.
On the main screen, select Wash on the user interface.
Once completed, remove the chip from the instrument.
Wipe down the electrodes with water and a lint-free swab.
Store the chip at 4 °C.
Open the instrument analysis software.
Go to File>Import Data File... and click on the desired *.gxd file.
Rename the wells using Tools > Sample Name Editor if necessary.
Select files to be exported by holding down shift while selecting them.
Click File>Export… and select the Raw Data box and then the AIA Format box.
Open the Browse Projects tab within the analysis software.
Go to Database>Import Data… and select the exported *.CDF files.
Dissolve 59.45 mg of Asn, 59.00 mg of Hyp, 65.77 mg of Gln, and 91.95 mg of Trp in 25 mL of 0.1 N HCl to prepare the extended amino acid (EAA) mixture.
Dissolve 58.58 mg of Nva and 44.54 mg of Sar in 50 mL of HCl to prepare the internal standard (ISTD) stock solution.

Combine the amino acid stock solution containing Ala, Asp, Arg, Cys, Glu, Gly, His, Ile, Leu, Met, Phe, Pro, Ser, Thr, Trp, Tyr, Val at 1 nmol/µL each with the EAA mixture for final concentrations of 900, 225, 90, 22.5, and 9 pmol/µL.
Add the prepared ISTD stock to the amino acid standards for a final concentration of either 90 pmol/µL or 900 pmol/µL to create "low" and "high" internal standards as positive controls.
Place the amino acid concentrations in sample vials into the autosampler of the UPLC.
Generate a calibration curve (9 to 900 pmol/µL) based on the amino acid standard concentrations using instrument software instructions.
Set up the Q-ToF in electrospray ionization (ESI) positive sensitivity mode coupled with a UPLC for intact amino acid analysis.
Prepare buffer A as acetonitrile + 0.1% formic acid and buffer B as 100 mM ammonium formate.
Set the LC flow rate to 0.6 mL/min.
Set the column temperature to 40 °C.
Use a normal phase column made for amino acid separations for chromatographic separation.
Apply a 15-minute gradient condition: 14% B (0-3 min), 14-100% B (3-10 min), 100% B (10-13 min), 100-8% B (13-14 min), 8% B (14-15 min).
Use the "Sample Type" and "Conc A" column listings in the MS acquisition program to create a calibration curve.
Right-click on the top menu bar and select Customize Display… to make the columns appear.
Enter "Standard" for the Sample Type of amino acid standards.
Enter "Analyte" for the media samples' Sample Type.
Fill in the "Conc A" column with the numerical concentrations of the standards in the required units (e.g., pmol/μL).
Run each prepared amino acid standard concentration at least twice.
Check the ISTD peaks to validate that the UPLC instrument and mass spectrometer are working properly.
Use the Edit Method option in the quantitation application to create a quantitation method (*.mdb file).
Define all amino acids of interest, including compound name, m/z value, and expected retention time.
Adjust the integration parameters for the method as necessary.
Apply the created amino acid method on standard samples to generate the calibration curve.
Export the calibration curve to a *.cdb file using Export>Calibration… for future use with media samples.
Save the desired layout to a *.qlt file using Save Layout As… in the quantitation application.
Centrifuge crude bioreactor media at 1,962 x g for 5 minutes.
Pass the centrifuged media through a 0.22 µm filter.
Mix the filtered media with 0.4 N HClO4 in a 1:1 ratio.
Centrifuge the mixed solution at 14,700 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Collect the clarified media in autosampler vials.
Run media samples in triplicate by LC-MS.
Use "Process Samples" under the quantitation program with the method (*.mdb) and calibration file (*.cdb).
Export data for analysis using the "Print" command, creating an *.xps or *.pdf file.
